core_summary: This expository text outlines yoga as an ancient Indian discipline derived from the Sanskrit root 'yuj' (to join), symbolizing the harmony of mind, body, thought, and action. It details how Sage Patanjali codified yoga philosophy in the 'Yoga Sutras' to quiet mental distractions. Practicing asanas requires coordinating physical postures with conscious breath control (pranayama) and present-moment focus. Daily practice increases flexibility, posture, and immunity while reducing stress and test anxiety. Modern tools like the WHO mYoga app broaden global access to these practices.
key_concepts: Mind-Body Unity: Harmonizing mental attention with physical posture and respiratory regulation.
Codification of Ancient Wisdom: Systematizing oral traditions into accessible philosophical texts.
Holistic Health Promotion: Enhancing physical immunity, posture, and mental calm simultaneously.
Global Accessibility via Digital Tools: Utilizing modern applications to distribute traditional health disciplines.

key_terms.definition: The practice of conscious breath control in yoga discipline.
A concise aphorism or rule in classical Indian philosophy.
The ability to withstand hardship or sustain prolonged physical effort.
The body's natural ability to resist infections and diseases.

key_takeaways: Yoga is a comprehensive lifestyle practice rather than mere physical stretching.
Combining breath control with posture strengthens physical health and mental focus.
Regular wellness habits build long-term stress resilience and emotional calm.
Ancient traditional wisdom remains highly relevant for modern well-being.
